Both well_formed_join_size and its proven copy pass handle is_short_string first, counting or writing inline payload bytes. direct_string handles only the remaining heap-string case; pointer_tagged_string rejects non-pointer tags before checking allocator ownership. A declined size proof takes the ordinary join path. Re-audited 2026-11-02: both passes now test the exact heap STRING_TAG first (the is_string arm of direct_string) and read that header; inline strings carry a different tag and still reach the is_short_string arm, so no inline payload is dereferenced as a header.

Only an entry whose upper 16 bits equal STRING_TAG>>48 (a heap string) is masked and read as a StringHeader. An inline-string entry carries SHORT_STRING_TAG, skips that branch and is compared by the masked-tail equality below, so no inline payload is dereferenced as a header; the query side is already split into StrKey::Short and StrKey::Heap.

Only a part tagged exactly 0x7FFF (STRING_TAG) that passes is_valid_string_ptr is read as a StringHeader. Inline strings carry SHORT_STRING_TAG, miss that arm and the number/int32 arms, and reach js_jsvalue_to_string, which materializes a heap string that is then rooted; no inline payload is dereferenced as a header.
